title: Finite-pushforward embeddings over a field
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a field [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/N$-modules on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], with the finite coefficient ring $\mathbf Z/N$ as in that definition. There are finitely many finite maps $h_i:Y_i\to X$, finite abelian groups $M_i$ killed by $N$, and an injective map of $\mathbf Z/N$-module sheaves
$$F\longrightarrow\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline M_i.$$
Here $\underline M_i$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] with its $\mathbf Z/N$-module structure, and direct images have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text: Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/N$. The field spectrum is locally Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $1$). Since $X$ is locally of finite type over it, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $X$ locally Noetherian. Finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], so $X$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $X$ is also quasi-separated. No separatedness of $X$ is assumed.

Fix $x\in X$, and write $b:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. By [prop-constructible-pullback], $b^{-1}F$ is constructible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-field-finite-separable-constant] with $k=\kappa(x)$ and the finite ring $\Lambda$. It gives a finite separable extension $K/\kappa(x)$, a finite $\Lambda$-module $M$, and a module-sheaf isomorphism $\theta:a^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline M_K$, where $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ is the composite through $b$. The underlying additive group of $M$ is finite abelian and $NM=0$, since $N\cdot1=0$ in $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 095G, lemma-pullback-constructible; Tag 09Z6, lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant, proof first construction and part (3)

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{x\}}$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its underlying space is irreducible: two opens meeting that closure both contain its generic point $x$. Thus reducedness makes $Z$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Choose a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ of $X$ with each $R_j$ a finitely generated algebra over the base field, as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Its intersections with $Z$ are $\operatorname{Spec}(R_j/I_j)$, a finite cover by finite-type field algebras, so $Z$ is of finite type over that field. The generic point of $Z$ is $x$, and its residue field is $\kappa(x)$: on an affine containing $x$, the closure has prime ideal $\mathfrak p_x$, and the generic local ring of $R/\mathfrak p_x$ is $\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p_x)=\kappa(x)$. Thus $K$ is a finite extension of the function field of $Z$, as required by the normalization-finiteness theorem. Use [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] for $X,x,K$: take its stated normalization of $Z$ in $K$. It gives a normal integral $Y$ and generic inclusion $e:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$, with function field $K$ and $a=he$. The morphism $Y\to Z$ is finite by [lem-fin-normalization-extension-finite]. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, its inverse image is the spectrum of an algebra finite as an $R/I$-module, where $R/I$ is the ring of $Z$ there. The same generators generate it as an $R$-module; hence $h:Y\to X$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Over the chosen finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}R_j$, these finite algebras are generated as field algebras by the generators of $R_j$ and their finite module generators. Their spectra form a finite affine cover of $Y$, hence $Y$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type over the field. Thus $Y$ is of finite type over the field and locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]; in particular it is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 09Z6, lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant, normalization construction and Nagata footnote; Morphisms Tags 035H, 035I, 035L and 01T6

proof.text: The natural map $u:\underline M_Y\to e_*\underline M_K$ is an isomorphism by [lem-fin-normal-generic-constant], applied to this normal integral Noetherian $Y$. It is $\Lambda$-linear: naturality with respect to multiplication by each scalar on $M$ says exactly that $u$ commutes with that scalar, and its inverse does too. Identify $e^{-1}h^{-1}F$ with $a^{-1}F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. Under the module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction], $\theta$ has an adjoint $\beta:h^{-1}F\to e_*\underline M_K$. Put $\alpha=u^{-1}\beta:h^{-1}F\to\underline M_Y$, and take its adjoint $\phi_x:F\to h_*\underline M_Y$. These are all maps of $\Lambda$-module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 09Z6, lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant, the two adjunctions; Tag 09Z5, lemma-push-constant-sheaf-from-open; Modules on Sites Tags 03D3 and 03D8

proof.text: The pullback $e^{-1}\alpha$ is an isomorphism. To see the precise map, let $v:e^{-1}\underline M_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline M_K$ be the canonical constant-pullback isomorphism [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. The natural map $u$ in step 4 is adjoint to $v$, so $\varepsilon_{e,\underline M_K}\,e^{-1}u=v$. The defining adjunction equation for $\beta$ says $\varepsilon_{e,\underline M_K}\,e^{-1}\beta=\theta$. Since $\beta=u\alpha$, these identities give $v\,e^{-1}\alpha=\theta$. Both $v$ and $\theta$ are isomorphisms, hence so is $e^{-1}\alpha$. These equations are the unit-counit identities for [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], in the module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction].

proof.text: Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be any geometric point with image $x$. Embed $K$ into $\Omega$ over $\kappa(x)$: choose finitely many algebraic generators of $K$, and extend the embedding successively by choosing a root in the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ of each generator's minimal polynomial. This gives $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K\xrightarrow{e}Y$ with $h\bar y=\bar x$. The stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] for $e$ and the isomorphism $e^{-1}\alpha$ of step 5 imply that $\alpha_{\bar y}$ is an isomorphism. Write $r:(h_*\underline M_Y)_{\bar x}\to(\underline M_Y)_{\bar y}$ for the germ restriction of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction]. Since $\phi_x=h_*\alpha\,\eta_{h,F}$, its composition with $r$ is $\alpha_{\bar y}$ after the canonical identification $F_{\bar x}\cong(h^{-1}F)_{\bar y}$. Indeed a representative section $s\in F(U)$ goes by the unit to its pullback on $U\times_XY$, then by $\alpha$ to its image there, and $r$ takes its germ at $(\bar u,\bar y)$; the unit-germ identity in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the first germ with $s_{\bar x}$. Therefore $r(\phi_x)_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism, and $(\phi_x)_{\bar x}$ is injective.

proof.text: Choose this construction for each point $x$ of $X$. At every geometric point over $x$, the associated $\phi_x$ is injective by step 6. Forgetting the module actions, $F$ is a constructible abelian sheaf: its finite locally constant module restrictions remain finite locally constant abelian restrictions [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-noetherian-finite-selection] to the family of these maps on the Noetherian scheme $X$. It gives finitely many of them with a monomorphism $F\to\bigoplus_i(h_i)_*\underline M_i$. The finite-sum map is still $\Lambda$-linear because every component is linear. It is injective as a module-sheaf map: cancellation against it follows from cancellation on the underlying abelian-sheaf maps, whose equality is equality of the module-sheaf maps. Each $h_i$ is finite by step 3, and each $M_i$ is finite abelian and killed by $N$ by step 2. If $X$ is empty or $F=0$, the empty finite family gives the map to the zero sheaf, which is a monomorphism.
